topics.title: Coursework & Assessment Categories
topics.summary: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.1.1, assessments are categorized into four levels (Category A: AI Prohibited, Category B: AI Minimal, Category C: AI Permitted, Category D: AI-Integrated) by Course Unit Directors and clearly stated in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3). Students may choose not to use AI for Categories A, B, and C without disadvantage, but this choice does not apply to Category D assessments which assess AI learning outcomes (§2.1.2). In Category A, all AI use including proofreading and text editing is prohibited; in Category B, AI is restricted to presentation only (fluency, grammar, spelling, formatting) without altering student ideas, arguments, or conclusions.
topics.scope: Undergraduate and postgraduate taught coursework assessments
actions: Check the designated AI category on your assessment brief on Canvas before beginning coursework.
If undertaking a Category B or C assessment, note that you may choose not to use AI tools personal to you.
Remember that Category D assessments require AI use to meet the unit's intended learning outcomes.

additionalTopics.summary: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).

title.zh: 曼彻斯特大学人工智能政策指南

scope.en: Official Senate policy (DocID 79331), 4-category assessment framework, Academic Malpractice Procedure (DocID 639), and approved tools guidance.
scope.zh: 覆盖曼彻斯特大学评议会政策（DocID 79331）、四级考核分类框架、《学术不端处理程序》（DocID 639）与大学核准 AI 工具的官方政策指南。

do.en: Always verify the designated AI assessment category (A, B, C, or D) in the course unit handbook and Canvas assessment brief before starting coursework (DocID 79331 §2.1.1, §2.1.3).
do.zh: 在开始任何课程作业前，务必查阅 Canvas 考核说明及课程大纲，核准依据 DocID 79331 §2.1.1 与 §2.1.3 明确标注的具体 AI 分类（A、B、C 或 D）。

do.en: Acknowledge AI use following University Library guidance: cite direct text/image use formally, provide an overview acknowledgement when asked or appropriate, and include prompts/outputs in an appendix when referencing AI as personal communication or required by School instructions.
do.zh: 遵循大学图书馆指南对 AI 使用进行规范引用与致谢：直接使用 AI 文本或图像须按规范正式引用；在被要求或适当时于文首或脚注提供致谢概述；当作为个人通信引用或学院有要求时，附上包含提示词与输出的附录。

do.en: Use your University IT account to access Microsoft Copilot Chat for commercial data protection; if uploading taught session recordings for study assistance, use University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot (DocID 79331 §2.2.2).
do.zh: 使用大学统一身份账户登录 Microsoft Copilot Chat 以享受商业数据保护；若需上传课程录像辅助学习，须依据 DocID 79331 §2.2.2 使用学校提供的 Microsoft 365 Copilot。

dont.en: Never upload University copyright materials—including lecture recordings, slides, handouts, and exam questions—to external AI tools (DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c)); teaching staff handling student-identifiable data must exclusively use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1).
dont.zh: 依据 DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c)，严禁向外部 AI 工具上传属于曼大版权的材料（包括课程录像、课件、讲义与试卷）；在教学活动中处理可识别学生身份数据的教职工必须专设使用学校提供的 M365 Copilot（§2.3.1）。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in Category A (Prohibited) assessments (even for proofreading or spelling/grammar correction), or beyond surface presentation in Category B (Minimal); note that student choice not to use AI does not apply to Category D (Integrated).
dont.zh: 严禁在类别 A（严禁使用）考核中使用任何生成式 AI（包括校对润色或语法拼写纠正）；在类别 B（最低限度）中严禁超越表层排版呈现去改动论点观点；同时注意 §2.1.2 赋予的不使用 AI 选择权不适用于类别 D（深度融合）。

dont.en: Do not present unacknowledged AI-generated content as your own (an indicator of academic malpractice under DocID 639 §3.1.3.6); markers rely on academic judgement and Turnitin similarity as the University does not use software claiming to detect GenAI (§4.2.2).
dont.zh: 切勿将未经披露的 AI 生成内容作为个人成果提交（属 DocID 639 §3.1.3.6 明确的学术不端指标）；评卷人依靠学术判断与 Turnitin 相似度比对，大学依据 §4.2.2 明确不使用声称能检测生成式 AI 的软件。

coursework.en: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.1.1, assessments are categorized into four levels (Category A: AI Prohibited, Category B: AI Minimal, Category C: AI Permitted, Category D: AI-Integrated) by Course Unit Directors and clearly stated in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3). Students may choose not to use AI for Categories A, B, and C without disadvantage, but this choice does not apply to Category D assessments which assess AI learning outcomes (§2.1.2). In Category A, all AI use including proofreading and text editing is prohibited; in Category B, AI is restricted to presentation only (fluency, grammar, spelling, formatting) without altering student ideas, arguments, or conclusions.
coursework.zh: 根据评议会政策 DocID 79331 §2.1.1，课程单元主管将考核划分为四个等级（类别 A：严禁使用 AI；类别 B：最低限度使用 AI；类别 C：允许使用 AI；类别 D：深度融合 AI），并在单元大纲及 Canvas 考核说明中予以明确公布（§2.1.3）。学生在类别 A、B、C 考核中可自主选择不使用 AI 且不受任何劣势对待，但该选择权不适用于专门考核 AI 学习成果的类别 D 考核（§2.1.2）。在类别 A 中，严禁一切 AI 使用（包括校对润色与文字编辑）；在类别 B 中，AI 使用严格限制于排版呈现层面（表达流畅度、语法、拼写、格式），严禁改变学生的观点、论据或结论。

exams.en: Examinations and timed assessments are categorized individually under the four-category framework (DocID 79331 §2.1.1). Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §3.1.2.5 and §4.3.1, students must adhere strictly to examination conditions communicated before the exam, and possessing or using unauthorized AI tools or online materials in examination sittings constitutes academic malpractice.
exams.zh: 考试与限时考核均在四级分类框架下逐一明确归类（DocID 79331 §2.1.1）。根据《学术不端处理程序》DocID 639 §3.1.2.5 及 §4.3.1，学生必须严格遵守考前公布的考场纪律与考试条件，在考场内持有或使用未经授权的 AI 工具或在线材料均构成学术不端行为。

disclosure.en: Under University Library referencing guidance, students must cite generative AI tools when using text or images directly in their work following 'Cite them Right' conventions. Where asked or deemed appropriate, students should include an overview acknowledgement at the start of work or in a footnote. An appendix detailing relevant prompts, outputs, generation dates, and modification statements is required when referencing AI as personal communication or when instructed by School guidance. Using tools for basic grammar and spell checking does not require acknowledgement unless School guidance requires it.
disclosure.zh: 根据大学图书馆参考文献指引，学生在作业中直接使用 AI 生成的文本或图像时，必须遵循“Cite them Right”规范正式引用。在有要求或适当时，学生应在作业开头或脚注中提供致谢概述。当将 AI 作为个人通信引用或学院指引有要求时，须附上详细记录相关提示词、输出内容、生成日期及修改说明的附录。仅使用工具进行基本语法与拼写检查无需致谢，除非学院指引另有特别规定。

privacy_data.en: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c), students must not upload University-owned copyright materials (such as lecture recordings, slides, handouts, or examination questions) to external commercial AI tools. Under §2.2.2, students are explicitly permitted to upload session recordings into University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot for study support. Under §2.3.1, staff members who use AI in Teaching and Learning activities must adhere to the University's AI Guidelines, and only the University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot service may be used for student-identifiable or confidential data.
privacy_data.zh: 根据评议会政策 DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c)，学生严禁将属于大学版权的材料（如课程录像、课件幻灯片、讲义或考试试题）上传至外部商业 AI 工具。根据 §2.2.2，明确允许学生将课堂录音录像上传至学校提供的 Microsoft 365 Copilot 开展学习辅助。根据 §2.3.1，在教学活动中使用 AI 的教职员工必须遵守大学 AI 指南，且仅可使用学校提供的 Microsoft 365 Copilot 服务处理涉及学生可识别身份或机密的数据。

approved_tools.en: The University provides Microsoft Copilot Chat with Commercial Data Protection to all active students and staff using University credentials. Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is deploying in phased license cohorts across 65,000 colleagues and students. NebulaONE is provided as an enterprise cloud AI development sandbox. Under DocID 79331 §2.1.1 and §2.2.1, having access to institutional AI tools does not confer permission to use them in Category A assessments.
approved_tools.zh: 大学面向全体在校师生通过统一认证提供具备商业数据保护的 Microsoft Copilot Chat。Microsoft 365 Copilot 套件正在面向 65,000 名师生员工分批分阶段部署。同时提供 NebulaONE 作为企业级云端 AI 开发沙箱。根据 DocID 79331 §2.1.1 与 §2.2.1，拥有机构 AI 工具的访问权限并不构成在类别 A 考核中使用的许可。

research_publication.en: Under StaffNet Research Guidelines, any use of AI to synthesise research data must be completely transparent, and fabricating or falsifying data with AI constitutes research misconduct. Corresponding authors carry ultimate responsibility for publication credibility and must declare significant AI assistance. Researchers reviewing papers or grants must preserve peer review confidentiality and never upload unpublished manuscripts into external AI services.
research_publication.zh: 根据 StaffNet 科研指引，使用 AI 合成研究数据必须完全公开透明，利用 AI 伪造或篡改数据构成科研不端。通讯作者对出版物的可信度承担最终责任，且必须披露重大 AI 辅助情况。参与论文或科研基金评审的研究人员必须严格保守同行评议机密，绝不得将未发表的手稿上传至外部 AI 服务。

academic_integrity.en: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).
academic_integrity.zh: 大学目前不使用声称能够检测生成式 AI 的软件；仅凭 Turnitin 相似度不能认定学术不端，必须依靠学术判断。根据《学术不端处理程序》DocID 639 §4.4.2，当存在代写嫌疑但缺乏直接证据，或现有信息无法达到盖然性优势标准时，经与学院主管官员商定可安排口头答辩（viva voce）以证明作者身份；该答辩不计入课程成绩。若举行答辩，通常不应晚于考核反馈截止日后 30 个工作日（§4.4.3.1）；学生应至少提前 5 个工作日收到说明答辩性质、目的及潜在结果的通知（§4.4.3.2）。学生选择的陪同人员仅可提供支持而不得发言参与（§4.4.3.4），且须提供合理调适（§4.4.3.5）。答辩本身不能直接作出处分（§4.4.4.2）；案件处理须遵循相应的 AUO/SDP/UDP 程序（§5.1–5.5）。

teaching_guidance.en: Senate Policy DocID 79331 and Faculty guidance mandate that Course Unit Directors specify AI categories in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3), establish group work logging rules and require prior peer consent before recording group discussions (§2.1.4–2.1.5), and require teaching staff handling student-identifiable data to use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1). Faculty guidance (FSE, BMH) supplements central policy.
teaching_guidance.zh: 评议会政策 DocID 79331 及各学院指引规定，课程单元主管必须在单元大纲与 Canvas 说明中明确标注 AI 分类（§2.1.3），建立小组作业日志规则并要求在录制小组讨论前获得同伴事先同意（§2.1.4–2.1.5），且要求处理学生可识别身份数据的教学人员专设使用 M365 Copilot（§2.3.1）。各学部指引（FSE、BMH）对全校政策作进一步补充。

security_procurement.en: IT Services and Information Governance establish clear tenant boundaries for Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and NebulaONE cloud sandbox, ensuring user authentication, commercial data encryption, and exclusion of university data from public LLM training.
security_procurement.zh: IT 服务部与信息管治团队为 Copilot Chat、Microsoft 365 Copilot 及 NebulaONE 云端沙箱确立了明确的租户安全边界，确保用户身份认证、商业数据加密，并严格防止大学数据被用于公开大语言模型的训练。

CL-001.text: The University of Manchester does not ban generative AI. The university's position is that when used appropriately, AI tools have the potential to enhance teaching and learning, and can support inclusivity and accessibility.
CL-001.scope: Institutional baseline policy position across all academic activities

evidence.quote: The University position is that, when used appropriately, AI tools have the potential to enhance teaching and learning and can support inclusivity and accessibility. Output from AI systems must be treated in the same manner by staff and students as work created by another person or persons, used critically and with permitted license, and cited and acknowledged appropriately.

evidence.quote:
The University has adopted the following principles, building on existing frameworks for academic integrity and emerging guidance on AI.
All staff and students using or developing AI are personally responsible for adhering to these.

topicBasis.coursework: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.1.1, assessments are categorized into four levels (Category A: AI Prohibited, Category B: AI Minimal, Category C: AI Permitted, Category D: AI-Integrated) by Course Unit Directors and clearly stated in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3). Students may choose not to use AI for Categories A, B, and C without disadvantage, but this choice does not apply to Category D assessments which assess AI learning outcomes (§2.1.2). In Category A, all AI use including proofreading and text editing is prohibited; in Category B, AI is restricted to presentation only (fluency, grammar, spelling, formatting) without altering student ideas, arguments, or conclusions.
topicBasis.exams: Examinations and timed assessments are categorized individually under the four-category framework (DocID 79331 §2.1.1). Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §3.1.2.5 and §4.3.1, students must adhere strictly to examination conditions communicated before the exam, and possessing or using unauthorized AI tools or online materials in examination sittings constitutes academic malpractice.
topicBasis.disclosure: Under University Library referencing guidance, students must cite generative AI tools when using text or images directly in their work following 'Cite them Right' conventions. Where asked or deemed appropriate, students should include an overview acknowledgement at the start of work or in a footnote. An appendix detailing relevant prompts, outputs, generation dates, and modification statements is required when referencing AI as personal communication or when instructed by School guidance. Using tools for basic grammar and spell checking does not require acknowledgement unless School guidance requires it.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c), students must not upload University-owned copyright materials (such as lecture recordings, slides, handouts, or examination questions) to external commercial AI tools. Under §2.2.2, students are explicitly permitted to upload session recordings into University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot for study support. Under §2.3.1, staff members who use AI in Teaching and Learning activities must adhere to the University's AI Guidelines, and only the University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot service may be used for student-identifiable or confidential data.
topicBasis.approved_tools: The University provides Microsoft Copilot Chat with Commercial Data Protection to all active students and staff using University credentials. Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is deploying in phased license cohorts across 65,000 colleagues and students. NebulaONE is provided as an enterprise cloud AI development sandbox. Under DocID 79331 §2.1.1 and §2.2.1, having access to institutional AI tools does not confer permission to use them in Category A assessments.
topicBasis.research_publication: Under StaffNet Research Guidelines, any use of AI to synthesise research data must be completely transparent, and fabricating or falsifying data with AI constitutes research misconduct. Corresponding authors carry ultimate responsibility for publication credibility and must declare significant AI assistance. Researchers reviewing papers or grants must preserve peer review confidentiality and never upload unpublished manuscripts into external AI services.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Senate Policy DocID 79331 and Faculty guidance mandate that Course Unit Directors specify AI categories in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3), establish group work logging rules and require prior peer consent before recording group discussions (§2.1.4–2.1.5), and require teaching staff handling student-identifiable data to use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1). Faculty guidance (FSE, BMH) supplements central policy.
topicBasis.security_procurement: IT Services and Information Governance establish clear tenant boundaries for Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and NebulaONE cloud sandbox, ensuring user authentication, commercial data encryption, and exclusion of university data from public LLM training.

approved_tools.en: The University provides Microsoft Copilot Chat with Commercial Data Protection to all active students and staff using University credentials. Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is deploying in phased license cohorts across 65,000 colleagues and students. NebulaONE is provided as an enterprise cloud AI development sandbox. Under DocID 79331 §2.1.1 and §2.2.1, having access to institutional AI tools does not confer permission to use them in Category A assessments.
approved_tools.zh: 大学面向全体在校师生通过统一认证提供具备商业数据保护的 Microsoft Copilot Chat。Microsoft 365 Copilot 套件正在面向 65,000 名师生员工分批分阶段部署。同时提供 NebulaONE 作为企业级云端 AI 开发沙箱。根据 DocID 79331 §2.1.1 与 §2.2.1，拥有机构 AI 工具的访问权限并不构成在类别 A 考核中使用的许可。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Institutionally procured and hosted software environments
approved_tools.meaningZh: 全校统一采购与托管的软件环境

research_publication.en: Under StaffNet Research Guidelines, any use of AI to synthesise research data must be completely transparent, and fabricating or falsifying data with AI constitutes research misconduct. Corresponding authors carry ultimate responsibility for publication credibility and must declare significant AI assistance. Researchers reviewing papers or grants must preserve peer review confidentiality and never upload unpublished manuscripts into external AI services.
research_publication.zh: 根据 StaffNet 科研指引，使用 AI 合成研究数据必须完全公开透明，利用 AI 伪造或篡改数据构成科研不端。通讯作者对出版物的可信度承担最终责任，且必须披露重大 AI 辅助情况。参与论文或科研基金评审的研究人员必须严格保守同行评议机密，绝不得将未发表的手稿上传至外部 AI 服务。
research_publication.meaningEn: Postgraduate research, academic publications, data synthesis, and peer review
research_publication.meaningZh: 研究生科研、学术出版、数据合成与同行评议

academic_integrity.en: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).
academic_integrity.zh: 大学目前不使用声称能够检测生成式 AI 的软件；仅凭 Turnitin 相似度不能认定学术不端，必须依靠学术判断。根据《学术不端处理程序》DocID 639 §4.4.2，当存在代写嫌疑但缺乏直接证据，或现有信息无法达到盖然性优势标准时，经与学院主管官员商定可安排口头答辩（viva voce）以证明作者身份；该答辩不计入课程成绩。若举行答辩，通常不应晚于考核反馈截止日后 30 个工作日（§4.4.3.1）；学生应至少提前 5 个工作日收到说明答辩性质、目的及潜在结果的通知（§4.4.3.2）。学生选择的陪同人员仅可提供支持而不得发言参与（§4.4.3.4），且须提供合理调适（§4.4.3.5）。答辩本身不能直接作出处分（§4.4.4.2）；案件处理须遵循相应的 AUO/SDP/UDP 程序（§5.1–5.5）。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Academic malpractice indicators, detector prohibition, optional authorship viva voce (§4.4.2–4.4.4), and AUO / SDP / UDP routing (§5.1–5.5)
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 学术不端指标、检测器禁用、可选作者身份口头答辩（§4.4.2–4.4.4）与 AUO/SDP/UDP 转介程序（§5.1–5.5）

teaching_guidance.en: Senate Policy DocID 79331 and Faculty guidance mandate that Course Unit Directors specify AI categories in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3), establish group work logging rules and require prior peer consent before recording group discussions (§2.1.4–2.1.5), and require teaching staff handling student-identifiable data to use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1). Faculty guidance (FSE, BMH) supplements central policy.
teaching_guidance.zh: 评议会政策 DocID 79331 及各学院指引规定，课程单元主管必须在单元大纲与 Canvas 说明中明确标注 AI 分类（§2.1.3），建立小组作业日志规则并要求在录制小组讨论前获得同伴事先同意（§2.1.4–2.1.5），且要求处理学生可识别身份数据的教学人员专设使用 M365 Copilot（§2.3.1）。各学部指引（FSE、BMH）对全校政策作进一步补充。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: Curriculum design, assessment briefs, group work consent, and staff instructional data protection
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 课程设计、考核任务说明、小组作业同意与教工教学数据保护

security_procurement.en: IT Services and Information Governance establish clear tenant boundaries for Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and NebulaONE cloud sandbox, ensuring user authentication, commercial data encryption, and exclusion of university data from public LLM training.
security_procurement.zh: IT 服务部与信息管治团队为 Copilot Chat、Microsoft 365 Copilot 及 NebulaONE 云端沙箱确立了明确的租户安全边界，确保用户身份认证、商业数据加密，并严格防止大学数据被用于公开大语言模型的训练。
security_procurement.meaningEn: Enterprise cloud boundaries, NebulaONE governance gateway, and data protection standards
security_procurement.meaningZh: 企业级云边界、NebulaONE 管治网关与数据保护标准
